name: app-frame
title: App frame
description: An app's panel inside its card (D-047): a sandboxed frame with an opaque origin (sandbox="allow-scripts" only) on the board's panel route, at the panel's size, which talks to the board only by the panel protocol: JSON-RPC 2.0 over postMessage in MCP Apps' shape (docs/specification/apps.md § The panel protocol). The page makes the frame only while its card is on screen and near enough to use (load / unload); until then it is a light placeholder with the app's title.

files.core: app-frame-core.ts (createAppBridge: the handshake, tools/call forwarding, escape, host-context-changed, JSON-RPC checks and errors, the message and call caps; panelSize, hostContext, hostStyles, parsePanelMessage, PROBLEM_WORDS, FRAME_CALLS; no DOM)
files.element: vb-app-frame.ts (defineVbAppFrame, VbAppFrameElement, AppFrameWiring, readLook; light DOM; the route is packages/format APP_PANEL_PATH)
files.styles: app-frame.css (scoped by the tag; tokens only; the size from --app-w and --app-h)

parts.vb-af-ph: the placeholder (aria-hidden: the card's name and the frame's title say it): the app's icon in its kind colour (vb-af-icon), its title (vb-af-title) and, while loading, 'Loading…' (vb-af-wait)
parts.vb-af-frame: the <iframe>, made by load(): sandbox="allow-scripts", src /app-panels/<id>, title the app's name, referrerpolicy no-referrer; hidden until the panel says it is ready (ui/notifications/initialized) or 1.5 s after it loaded

attributes.data-app: the app's id (APP_ID); the frame is made only for an id that fits, and a new one starts the panel again
attributes.data-label: the app's name: the placeholder's title and the frame's title
attributes.data-w, data-h: the panel's size in px, held to APP_SIZE (panelSize); set as --app-w and --app-h through the CSSOM; a change tells a ready panel (host-context-changed)
attributes.data-state: idle | loading | ready (set by the element)
attributes.data-focus-in: focus is inside the panel (set by the element from the window's blur and focus: Chromium never matches :focus-within on a frame of another origin); the frame draws the focus ring
attributes.aria-busy: true while loading (set by the element)

methods.wire({ callTool, look?, onEscape? }): once: the page's call_app_tool through its I/O layer, the board's look (left out: readLook, the tokens resolved through a probe, the theme from the card surface) and what Esc in the panel does (left out: focus the card)
methods.load(): make the frame and its protocol bridge, and listen for messages; nothing while loaded, not in the page, or for a bad id
methods.unload(): remove the frame, close the bridge, stop listening; focus in the panel goes back to the card; also on disconnect
methods.lookChanged(): the board's theme changed: a ready panel gets host-context-changed with the parts that changed

events: message on window: passed to the bridge, as the frame's only when event.source is this frame's window and event.origin is "null"; every other window's message is ignored
ui/notifications/escape from the panel -> onEscape (focus back to the card)
blur and focus on window while loaded: data-focus-in follows whether the frame is the page's active element
whenToUse: Inside an app card (kind app), which the node template draws it into.
whenNotToUse: Any other embedded content: Markdown never renders HTML (D-023), and nothing else on the board may run in a frame.
accessibility: The frame has a title naming the app, so a screen reader announces it on entry. Tab moves from the card into the panel and on out of it in the page's order; the panel is hidden (so not focusable) until it is ready. Esc in a panel that sends ui/notifications/escape (the example does) returns focus to the card; the board cannot see keys inside the panel, so a panel that sends none is left with Tab or Shift+Tab. The placeholder is aria-hidden; aria-busy marks the frame while it loads. Unloading a frame that holds focus moves focus to the card, never to the page's body.
